item.title: The timeout that might have worked: how to retry when you don't know if the first call landed
item.description: A timeout is not a failure. It’s an unknown, and retrying an unknown is how agents double-send emails and double-charge cards. A practical way to handle it: sort every tool into one of three classes, treat a timeout as a fourth outcome that needs its own branch, verify by reading the effect before you write again, and fall back to a reconciliation record when the tool gives you nothing to read.

item.title: What Idempotent Actually Means: Why Retries Are Safe (and When They Aren't)
item.description: Idempotent means doing something twice has the same effect as doing it once. This is essential for APIs, agents, and any system where retries can happen. Here’s why, and how to get it right.

item.title: Your retry just sent the email twice: idempotency keys for agents
item.description: Retrying a read is free. Retrying a write can charge a card twice, send two emails, or book two rooms — and the model has no idea it happened. Retry safety is a property you build into the tool, not a flag you set on the loop. Here’s why at-least-once delivery is the default you’re actually running, how to derive a stable idempotency key from an agent’s intent, and a dedup wrapper that makes any write safe to retry.
